content.text:
I have what I need. Let me analyze the direction and materials terms.

**Key findings:**
- Initial Term is **one (1) year**, auto-renewing in 1-year increments (p0016).
- No convenience right for either party during the Initial Term (only breach/insolvency under 4(b)).
- After the Initial Term, **either party** may terminate for any reason on **90 days' written notice**.
- No early-termination fee or acceleration; Kubient is only entitled to fees *generated* during the 90-day notice period (i.e., revenue actually earned for services rendered, not a penalty).
- Economics are a revenue share (p0023) — AP is not prepaying fees, so there is no prepaid-fee refund to claw back.

input.quote: Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement
input.rationale: This clause sits at the playbook fallback and is therefore acceptable without redline. (1) Customer convenience right: AP may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' written notice, which is within the fallback's 60–90 day band. The suspension of convenience termination during the Initial Term does not trigger the "missing behaviour" deviation because the Initial Term is exactly one (1) year, not longer than 12 months, and renewals are 1-year (not multi-year) periods, so this is not walk-away territory. (2) No early-termination penalty: there is no termination fee or acceleration of future fees; Kubient is entitled only to fees actually "generated during the termination period," i.e., revenue earned for services rendered during the 90-day notice window, well inside the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap. (3) Vendor convenience right: Kubient's mirror right requires ninety (90) days' notice and cannot be exercised during the Initial Term, so it is above the walk-away threshold of "fewer than 90 days." Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred position but are noted rather than flagged: Kubient's right runs at any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a term, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund mechanic. The refund point is immaterial here because Section 5 is a revenue-share arrangement (Kubient remits a share of auction revenue to AP) rather than a prepaid subscription, so AP has no prepaid fees at risk. Because the clause meets the fallback on every material term — notice length, absence of penalty, and Vendor notice period — no redline is proposed.
